questions.question_text: In South Dakota, residential closings are typically handled by:
questions.explanation: South Dakota closings are typically conducted by title companies or attorneys. They can take place at the broker's office, title company, or lending agency, and may be conducted as round-table (all parties present) or by mail/escrow.

questions.question_text: A closing where all parties are present at the same location is called a:
questions.explanation: South Dakota allows both round table closings (all parties present) and closings by mail or escrow. Round table closings allow immediate document signing, question answering, and fund transfers in a single meeting.

questions.question_text: Who owes South Dakota sales tax on the commission from a real estate sale?
questions.correct_answer: The broker, on the full commission received
distractors: The seller, as a closing cost
Each broker associate on their share of the split
No one — commissions are exempt from sales tax
questions.explanation: Commissions from the sale of South Dakota real property carry state and municipal sales tax based on where the property sits, and the broker owes it on the full commission with no deduction for splits. Broker associates owe nothing on their share.

questions.question_text: South Dakota property taxes are assessed one year and due the next. This system is called:
distractors: Taxes paid at point of sale
questions.explanation: Taxes are assessed one year and become due and payable January 1 of the next (SDCL 10-21-4). The first half runs penalty-free through April 30 and the second half through October 31, which is what closing prorations work from.

questions.question_text: A title search reveals a mechanic's lien on the property. This would be classified as a:
questions.correct_answer: Title defect that must be resolved before closing
distractors: Normal encumbrance that the buyer must accept
Matter only for the lender to address
questions.explanation: A mechanic's lien is a title defect — an encumbrance that would appear on the title search. Title companies examine recorded documents for liens, encumbrances, and defects to ensure clear title can be conveyed to the buyer at closing.

questions.question_text: What is the South Dakota real estate transfer fee rate?
questions.explanation: The transfer fee is 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of it — about 0.1 percent — and the grantor pays it (SDCL 43-4-21). The register of deeds collects it when the deed is recorded.

questions.question_text: Who is responsible for paying the real estate transfer fee in South Dakota?
questions.explanation: The grantor pays the transfer fee (SDCL 43-4-21). The register of deeds collects it at recording and stamps the amount in red ink on the face of the deed, and the proceeds go to the county general fund.

questions.question_text: South Dakota property taxes are paid in arrears. When are tax installments due?
questions.explanation: Property taxes are payable in two halves, the first through April 30 and the second through October 31 without penalty (SDCL 10-21-4). Because they are paid in arrears, the seller's share of the current year is usually credited to the buyer at closing.

questions.question_text: South Dakota follows which type of recording system?
questions.explanation: A conveyance is void against a later good-faith purchaser for value whose deed is recorded first (SDCL 43-28-17). Recording first only wins if that later buyer also took without notice, which is what makes the system race-notice rather than pure race.

questions.question_text: A government agency transfers property to another government entity. Is the transfer fee required?
questions.correct_answer: No, government transfers are exempt from the fee
distractors: Yes, all transfers require the full fee amount
Yes, but at a reduced rate of 50% of normal
No, but only federal government agencies qualify
questions.explanation: Transfers by or to the United States, this state, or any political subdivision are exempt (SDCL 43-4-22(2)). Every exempt deed must state 'exempt from transfer fee' and cite the subdivision claimed; falsifying value or an exemption is a Class 1 misdemeanor.
